flags.title: Unit 2 single-notice combined increase would exceed 10% — 90-day notice mandatory
flags.detail: If the owner imposed all banked increases (11.5%) plus the 2026-27 annual increase (1.6%) in one notice, the combined 13.1% increase exceeds 10% of the rent charged during the prior 12 months. California Civil Code §827(b)(3)(A) then requires at least 90 days' written notice (not 30). A 30-day notice would be defective. See S-12.
flags.action: Serve 90-day written notice, or phase increases across anniversaries (each ≤10% combined with proper notice), within AGA limits.

flags.title: HUD Fair Market Rent values for San Francisco could not be read from the official HUD page
flags.detail: HUDUSER's FMR page was reachable but the area-level FY2027 San Francisco figures are behind the FMR Query tool/downloads and could not be confirmed this session. Per the project's verification rule, FMR dollar values are published as blank/unverified. Secondary reporting (T-03) claims FY2027 2BR = $3,697 (FY2026 = $3,604) — unverified. S-19 and S-20 (federalregister.gov notice, effective 2026-10-01) remain the official entry points.
flags.action: Verify at https://www.huduser.gov/portal/datasets/fmr.html (FMR Query Tool) before citing any FMR figure.

flags.title: Unit 1 continuing-tenancy note (April 1, 2026) is ambiguous in the records reviewed
flags.detail: Records show the February 1, 2025 lease at $3,995 with initial occupants (placeholder Tenants A, B, C) and, from April 1, 2026, a continuing tenancy at $3,995 with current occupants (placeholder Tenants A, D). It is not documented whether occupants changed by move-out/move-in or otherwise. A new roommate may NOT be used as a basis for any added rent (S-01). If any occupant change occurred, no new agreement may set rent above the lawful rent plus AGA during the continuing tenancy.
flags.action: Confirm current occupants and lease status from the ledger; do not increase rent on account of occupancy changes alone.

flags.title: Whether Unit 1's $3,995 February 2025 rent was a lawful vacancy-decontrol market reset is unverified
flags.detail: Costa-Hawkins (Civil Code §1954.53) allows an owner to set the initial rent on a NEW tenancy; SF imposes no vacancy-control cap on the first rent of an emptied unit (S-01, S-15). The records do not show whether the February 1, 2025 commencement was a fresh tenancy following a voluntary vacancy, or a re-papering of an existing tenancy (which could NOT lawfully reset rent). If the prior tenancy was terminated by the owner, exceptions may apply (§1954.53(a)(1)).
flags.action: Confirm with the prior-tenancy file; if it was an owner-terminated tenancy, consult Rent Board/counsel before treating $3,995 as freely set.

flags.title: Unit 1's skipped 2025-26 (1.4%) increase is NOT yet bankable
flags.detail: SF.gov: a skipped increase is banked only once at least 24 full months pass without any rent increase. The tenancy began February 1, 2025 and no increase has been imposed; 24 full months elapse on February 1, 2027. Imposing a 'banked' 1.4% before February 1, 2027 would exceed the lawful amount for the notice date. (The 2026-27 1.6% annual increase remains available on/after March 1, 2026 with a 12-month-anniversary-compliant notice.) See S-04.
flags.action: Do not impound any banked increase until on/after February 1, 2027; date the Unit 1 increase notice accordingly.

flags.title: Secondary report: 2026-27 AGA (1.6%) allegedly computed via geometric-mean estimate of missing October 2025 CPI
flags.detail: A secondary source (T-02) reports the Rent Board used a geometric-mean estimate from August and December 2025 CPI in place of missing October 2025 CPI. No official page read this session confirms this methodology detail. Official pages (S-01, S-02, S-07, S-03) confirm only the result (1.6%) and the formula basis (60% of Bay Area CPI-U).
flags.action: If methodology matters for review, request the Rent Board's published determination/minutes; treat T-02 as unverified.

flags.title: Unit 2 current lawful base rent not confirmed — all Unit 2 amounts assume $3,150
flags.detail: Records show lease start June 1, 2019 at $3,150/month. Any subsequent lawful increases (annual or banked) would raise the base. If increases were imposed, Unit 2's banked capacity is lower than shown; if none were, banking is valid but requires the Rent Increase License and correct notice. $3,150 is used ONLY as the recorded lease-start rent, flagged unverified as the CURRENT base.
flags.action: Pull the full rent ledger and the Rent Board Housing Inventory report for Unit 2 before serving any notice; recompute from the lawful base.

flags.title: Anonymization applied sitewide
flags.detail: Every personal identifier is replaced with placeholders (Tenants A–F). Dates and dollar amounts are preserved exactly. No street address beyond 94122/Outer Sunset is published. The mapping lives only in the private source file, not in this repository.

flags.title: Prop F / Tenant Right to Counsel cited via official Form 1007; standalone official program page not read this session
flags.detail: The official SF Rent Board Form 1007 (S-11) states tenants facing eviction have access to the Tenant Right to Counsel Program and lists the Eviction Defense Collaborative intake ((415) 659-9184, legal@evictiondefense.org, 976 Mission Street). The city's standalone RTC webpage was not independently read; the program is referenced here only via S-10/S-11 and secondary T-04 (flagged).
flags.action: If a standalone citation is needed, confirm at SF.gov / SF Service Guide before publishing externally.

flags.title: Mail service adds 5 days (reconciled sources)
flags.detail: SF.gov pages state a mailed notice requires 5 more days (S-01, S-04). Civil Code §827(b)(2)–(3) incorporates CCP §1013 for mailed service (5 days within California). Consistent; the longer effective date governs. Personal delivery is the cleanest service method.
flags.action: Serve personally where feasible; if mailed, add 5 days and document the mailing date.

flags.title: Not legal advice; SF tenant protections are strict and tenants get free legal help
flags.detail: Any increase is scrutinized against Chapter 37, Civil Code §§827, 1946.2, 1947.12, 1954.53, FEHA §12955, Unruh §51 and the Fair Housing Act. Tenants facing eviction are entitled to free representation under the Tenant Right to Counsel Program (S-10, S-11); all tenants may call Rent Board counselors at (415) 252-4600 (S-05, S-10). This pack is analysis, not legal advice.
flags.action: Have a qualified attorney or Rent Board counselor review the actual notice before service.

flags.title: Process: single-session worker + integration; basis of verification
flags.detail: All official rows were read directly from .gov/.ca.gov/federalregister.gov pages on 2026-11-06. The HUD area-level FMR figures (F-R2) and the Unit 2 ledger (F-R7) are the only substantive facts not verifiable from official sources this session and are published blank/flagged accordingly.

flags.title: Market-practice section (corporations vs individual owners) rests on the legal framework, not market data
flags.detail: No official SF or federal dataset on corporate vs individual rent-increase behavior in 94122 could be read this session. The corporate/individual distinction is therefore presented ONLY as (a) the legal framework that treats owners differently in narrow cases (e.g., Civil Code §1947.12(d)(5): the single-family/condo AB 1482 exemption is lost for REIT/corporation/LLC owners), and (b) clearly labeled general practice observations with secondary sourcing flagged unverified. No market statistic is published.
flags.action: If market practice data is required, commission it from a verified dataset; do not cite aggregator blogs as authority.
